# Independent migration repair review

**Final review:** parent corrected R1 to the owner executable bit in both functions. Independent reexecution of all eight acceptance tests passed, including actual chmod0645 portability and0755→0655 rejection. The direct synthetic probe also now matches the separately observed Git semantics. No remaining actionable finding in this bounded patch; final full-suite/audit/release/actual-machine evidence remains parent-owned. Original finding and counterexample below are retained as history.

## Initial review, before parent correction

One actionable P2 remains in the reviewed portable acceptance change: the proposed digest treats **any** executable bit as Git executable identity. Git uses the owner executable bit. A fresh isolated Git index classified 0645/0654 as 100644, while `adoptionSourceContentSha256` classified them executable. Equal content at 0755 and 0655 also receives the same proposed digest even though owner execution is lost. Use `mode & 0o100`, align the existing `gitIdentity` comparison, and add mixed-bit controls. This finding concerns audit identity; it does not assert that strict transaction snapshots or every production clean-tree check can be bypassed.

[git-mode-probe.json](git-mode-probe.json) preserves actual Git observations from a temporary repository inside this review's owned directory, removed afterward without a commit. [digest-mode-probe.json](digest-mode-probe.json) demonstrates the original helper collision using synthetic equal-content snapshots. Neither probe invokes native managers or touches the user's installed packages.

The vendor-overlap correction is otherwise appropriately bounded. It deduplicates only the unrelated-name comparison set; full unrelated registration arrays and observed payload hashes remain in `unrelatedHash`. Managed-to-managed duplicates and managed-to-vendor conflicts still reject in observation and predicted exposure. The added actual isolated Codex/Pi tests first reproduce the original rejection, then perform withdrawal/exposure and compare unrelated config/payload hashes, and finally introduce a managed collision that must reject. Their original two failures and subsequent 19-pass log are retained. These are reviewed parent executions, not a new reviewer-run native test.

Schema2 otherwise preserves entry paths, kinds, byte lengths and content hashes; schema1 keeps its prior behavior. Missing/symlink source roots fail, and strict local snapshots retain permissions/inode/path identity for pre-effect revalidation. The added permission-portability test deliberately changes modes after its first receipt and verifies the old local snapshot rejects. Content, extra-path and format negatives remain. The source digest is a release identity function, not a replacement for local ownership/race snapshots.

The three changed production modules are all included among the ten newly bound implementation files. The assembler derives obligations from the production function and creates schema2 hashes with the same exported helper, then invokes the verifier for all package/host pairs. Its independent expected-tree test is valuable because assembler/verifier self-agreement alone would miss the executable-bit error. These ten files cover the declared repair; they are not a claim of complete transitive import coverage for every updater dependency.

Four passes: reviewed full changed source and surrounding observer/snapshot/caller boundaries; inspected actual native test setup and before/after logs; challenged normalization against actual Git and a direct helper counterexample; checked scope/wording and retained the finding. Final full-suite results, rebuilt audit, patch-release publication and actual machine effects remain parent-owned. No source repair, commit, model call or installed-host mutation was performed by this review.
